subject: Re: ZenWave — spikes in 5xx and p95 latency (us-west-2)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@zenwave.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@zenwave.io
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: High 5xx rate + p95 latency spike — us-west-2

Hi Mina / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and a sustained p95 latency spike for most of our traffic hitting us-west-2 beginning ~14:40 PDT. Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to 6–7% and p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.8s. This is impacting our customer-facing search and a few queued background jobs are timing out.

Attached is a short CSV with traces from 14:35–15:05 and a screenshot of the error-rate graph. Our ops team has already tried circuiting a small portion of traffic to us-west-1 but the client SDK pins regions aggressively and we continue to see requests routed to us-west-2.

We need an expedited mitigation plan and, if required, an executive-level routing decision (cross-region drain or failover). Please let me know immediate next steps and whether you can authorize a cross-region redirect while you investigate root cause. We have a weekly sync with our CTO at 10:00 PT tomorrow and need clarity before then.

—Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform — ZenWave
elena.torres@zenwave.io
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@zenwave.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 15:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate + p95 latency spike — us-west-2

Thanks for flagging this, Elena — and for the traces. I’m escalating internally and we’ll provide an immediate mitigation recommendation within 30 minutes.

Short plan:
- Rishi/SRE to validate whether surface-level throttling or a networking/glitch at our us-west-2 pool is responsible (collect KV cache stats + queue backpressure numbers).
- If we confirm a regional capacity/pathing issue and errors persist, request exec sign-off for temporary cross-region traffic steering (us-west-2 -> us-west-1) for up to 6 hours while we stabilize.
- Communications: We’ll prep an incident note and a short customer-facing update.

I’ve attached the log snapshot Elena sent for quick reference and looped in Vanessa for deal/credit impact and Marissa for CS comms.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 15:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate + p95 latency spike — us-west-2

Quick findings from the initial triage:
- Autoscale metrics for the us-west-2 dedicated pool show normal GPU utilization but a sudden spike in connection-level 5xx errors from the edge LB between 14:38–14:52.
- KV cache hit ratio dropped ~12% during the spike; a subset of high-QPS clients experienced cache churn.
- No obvious model degradation (weights/versions unchanged) but we see elevated RT tail correlated with edge retries.

Mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Short-term route steer (recommended): divert ~65% of prod traffic to us-west-1 for 2–4 hours. Pros: stabilizes customer traffic quickly; Cons: increased tail for pinned SDK clients and potential transient errors as clients reconnect.
2) Gradual canary drain: move 10–15% of traffic and increase if error-rate drops. Pros: safer for client pinning; Cons: may take longer to bring global error-rate down.
3) Wait + fix: deeper networking investigation (route tables/edge infra). Pros: root-cause-first; Cons: customer experience remains degraded and CS pressure grows.

Given ZenWave’s SLA sensitivity and the request for an exec decision, I recommend option (1) now and a follow-up canary validation after stabilization. If we approve (1), we need:
- Exec sign-off for cross-region steering (Marissa)
- Ops ticket to programmatically apply steer + rollback playbook (I’ll open PD incident and create a runbook fragment)
- CS statement drafted for customer-facing comms (Marissa / Vanessa)

I’ll attach a short runbook snippet and open the PagerDuty incident P12345.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Site Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 09:41:00 -0400
Subject: Re: High 5xx rate + p95 latency spike — us-west-2

Thanks team — I authorize the short-term cross-region steering (option 1) for up to 6 hours. Please proceed with the following:
- Rishi: initiate the 65% traffic steer to us-west-1 now, monitor error-rate and p95 every 5 minutes, and be ready to rollback if errors rise or new regressions appear.
- Mina: coordinate a concise customer update to Elena (30–60m target) explaining the mitigation and next steps.
- Vanessa: own any commercial remediation discussion (credits/contract impacts) and confirm whether we need Legal looped.
- Ops: open an incident timeline entry and collect post-mortem artifacts (edge LB logs, route table deltas, KV cache samples).

We will treat this as a P0 customer escalation — if the steer does not materially reduce the error/latency within 30 minutes, escalate to the executive on-call for broader fleet-level mitigation.

I’ll join the 10:00 PT sync with ZenWave if helpful; otherwise I’ll be on standby for approvals.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
